text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-4521 - cuda_mem_pressure_high on gpu-pool-eu-west - auto-pager triggered by metric rule (gpu.memory.used_pct > 92% for 2m). Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-4521

pagerduty: Alert details: rule=cuda_mem_pressure_high, severity=critical, host=gpu-node-12, pool=gpu-pool-eu-west, metric_peak=95.6%

amy (oncall): acked oncall. i'm taking this. i'll triage.

josh (infra): seeing a flurry of OOMs in kube logs for pod rserve-22, container=runtime-proxy. logs show cublas alloc errors + SIGBUS. past 3 mins.

amy (oncall): copy. can you drop nvidia-smi + dmesg snippet? also which models were running?

josh (infra): pasting quick snippets:
```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv -l 1
index, name, utilization.gpu [%], memory.used [MiB], memory.total [MiB]
0, NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB, 98 %, 39312 MiB, 40536 MiB
1, NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB, 95 %, 38720 MiB, 40536 MiB
```

and dmesg shows repeated kernel message:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:5e:00): 79, pid=23456, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12346.123456] cgroup: process 23456 (python) tried to kill init
```

sean (eng-runtime): that Xid 79 is a memory access error, often correlated with kernel SIGBUS after cudnn/cublas alloc failures. could be fragmentation + large KV cache churn. any recent model rollouts?

amy (oncall): lia, any CS tickets? are customers seeing errors?

lia (cs): we have two customer error reports: customer A noted increased 500s on embedding endpoints starting ~09:02 UTC. severity: medium, specific tenants: cust-alpha, cust-beta. attaching their logs to the incident.

amy (oncall): quick mitigation plan: 1) scale down heavy model replicas on gpu-pool-eu-west 2) enable auto-evacuate on noisy pods 3) if needed, cordon node gpu-node-12 and drain. josh, can you identify top memory hog pods?

josh (infra): running a one-liner to list top gpu memory consumers:
```
kubectl -n inference top pod --containers | sort -k3 -nr | head -n 10
# shows runtime-proxy, quantizer-3, eval-worker-9 as top consumers
```

josh (infra): i can evict eval-worker-9 and quantizer-3 from pool to free ~22GB combined. ready to run if you want.

amy (oncall): do it. mark it in thread and watch. also increase pool surge capacity by +1 GPU node via autoscaler while we investigate.

ops-bot: Started eviction: pod=eval-worker-9 namespace=inference node=gpu-node-12 action=evict

josh (infra): eviction completed, freed ~11GB. quantizer-3 still heavy, draining it now.

ops-bot: Completed eviction: pod=eval-worker-9 status=evicted freed=11264MiB

sean (eng-runtime): adding a temp guardrail: set per-request token cap to 4k for large-model routes to avoid KV cache blowouts. applying config: /ops/configs/limits/temporal-token-cap.json

amy (oncall): good. monitor metrics. lia, update customer A: "We're mitigating GPU memory pressure, team has evicted heavy workers and increased capacity; you may see improved success rates in ~5-10m."

lia (cs): updated. customer acknowledged, will reopen if they still see failures.

josh (infra): after draining noisy pods, memory usage dipped to 78% on node-12. but we've seen a couple SIGBUS Xid 79s earlier - need to watch if node hardware is flaky.

sean (eng-runtime): runbook step next: if Xid 79 persists after freeing memory, reboot node and reprobe for hardware faults. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-memory-pressure

amy (oncall): agreed. not yet rebooting. continuing observation window 15m. connecting to oncall slack handoff: i'm scheduled out at 09:50 UTC; if unresolved by then, i'll hand to se an.

amy (oncall): notes for post-incident: collect per-pool KV cache growth graphs, correlate with heavy client sequences, and see if quantization config change last deploy increased memory. file for postmortem: #INC-4521.

josh (infra): filed support case with cloud vendor to flag possible HW recurrences; ticket #CLD-9981.

incident-bot: PagerDuty escalation status: acked by amy (oncall) at 09:08 UTC, no further escalation.

lia (cs): customer A confirmed errors dropped to 0 after mitigation, they say latencies returned to normal.

ops-bot: autoscaler bumped pool gpu-pool-eu-west by +1 node: node=gpu-node-15 status=provisioned

amy (oncall): wrapping up initial mitigation. current status: mem usage stable ~72-80%, no new OOMs in last 6m, customers reporting recovered. i'll continue monitoring until handoff at 09:50.

sean (eng-runtime): follow-ups for next 24h: 1) capture heap snapshots from runtime-proxy, 2) add more aggressive kv-cache trimming thresholds under memory pressure, 3) run fragmentation probe job on pool.

amy (oncall): thanks team. leaving this thread open. if anything new pops, call PD.

josh (infra): thumbs up :thumbsup:

lia (cs): ty all, will ping if customers reopen.

amy (oncall): handoff note at 09:50 UTC -> se an: passing monitor duties. summary: evicted noisy pods, added node, customers recovered, possible Xid79 hardware signal under observation. full context + logs: https://redwood.internal/incidents/PD-4521/logs

sean (eng-runtime): taking over at 09:50 UTC. acked.

incident-bot: thread closed for new automated alerts; manual updates allowed.
